schemes.description: Level 6 Kent Business School module (Medway, Summer Term) in which groups of KBS students act as consultants on live problems set by real businesses. 2026 cohort: 106 students in 15 consultancy teams across 10 live projects over eight weeks, visiting business sites and meeting senior business representatives, producing recommendations presented back to the organisation.
schemes.eligible_faculties_programmes: KBS students (Canterbury and Medway) at Stage 3; blog reports students from across KBS
schemes.eligibility_restrictions: Search summary reported an average of at least 60% in the preceding stage; module page fetched did not state a restriction (conflict, unresolved).
schemes.credit_assessment: 20 credits (10 ECTS). Group report 3,000 words 60%; group presentation 15 min 20%; individual reflective blog 750 words 20%.
schemes.project_evidence: Live business challenges; group report and presentation with recommendations [1][2].
schemes.group_evidence: 'in a group of your peers'; group report and group presentation assessed; 15 teams in 2026 [1][2].
schemes.employer_evidence: Four external organisations supported the projects; teams visited sites, engaged senior business representatives and produced recommendations 'presented back to the organisation' [2]. Module page: 'we'll work with real businesses' [1].
schemes.partner_role: Sets live challenge; engages with teams on site; receives recommendations/presentation
schemes.named_partners: Port of Dover, Macknade, Barretts Kent, Enterprise Mobility (2026 cohort) [2]
schemes.deliverable: Group consultancy report and client presentation
schemes.unresolved: Whether compulsory on any KBS degree (page silent); progression threshold conflict; whether 'four external organisations' covered all 10 projects.

profile_md:
Kent's strongest verified route is the **KBS Challenge (BUSB6514)**: a Level 6, 20-credit Kent Business School module where groups consult for real businesses. In 2026, 106 students in 15 teams worked on 10 live projects over eight weeks for Port of Dover, Macknade, Barretts Kent and Enterprise Mobility, presenting recommendations back to the organisations; assessment is a group report and presentation plus individual blog. It meets all three criteria with 2026/27 evidence, but only KBS students are evidently eligible and it is not shown to be compulsory.

Other leads are weaker. **i-Teams** (Careers and Employability Service, multi-disciplinary teams, sponsor challenges, mentor, Grand Final) fits the criteria and is open beyond business students, but the latest evidenced cohort is 2023 and no current delivery was found. The **Business Analytics Challenge (BUSB7032)** and MSc **Strategic Project Management Challenge** are consultancy-style team modules whose client role is unclear. IT consultancy (KITC) modules involve external clients but are individually assessed and not running. Engineering and physics group projects show no confirmed external client; Law Clinic is casework. The legacy Employability Points scheme is an award, not a project route. Provision is distributed within business with one central extracurricular route; no institution-wide curricular scheme was found.
gaps: Compulsory status of KBS Challenge and its eligibility threshold; i-Teams current delivery; client role in BUSB7032 and Strategic Project Management Challenge; MSc International Business live consultancy; engineering/computing and Digital Arts projects with industry advisers (2019 pages only); further departmental instances likely. Reduced-depth: 11 searches, 12 fetches.
